seo.title: Amazon Redshift client for {devices}
seo.description: Query Redshift clusters and Serverless workgroups on the PostgreSQL driver. See DISTKEY and SORTKEY, browse external schemas and back up with pg_dump.

header.title: Amazon Redshift client
header.lead: Query provisioned clusters or Serverless workgroups, and inspect sort keys, distribution styles and external schemas.

bands.title: Connect
text: Enter a cluster or Serverless workgroup endpoint, port and database; clusters start with dev, and a redshift:// URL fills in the form. New connections set SSL to Preferred, and there is no version check, so any cluster AWS still runs connects.
The password is kept in the Keychain or read from ~/.pgpass. A cluster that is not publicly reachable is reached through an SSH tunnel to a bastion host in its VPC.

bands.title: Query and edit
text: Queries and row edits work as they do on <postgresql>PostgreSQL</postgresql>, through the same driver, and a tab bound to another database opens a second connection for it. <explain>EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN VERBOSE</explain> return Redshift’s plan as text.

Distribution style, sort keys and size come from svv_table_info, and DDL includes DISTKEY, SORTKEY, DISTSTYLE and ENCODE; foreign keys are listed, but Redshift does not enforce them. External Spectrum, federated, cross-database and datashare schemas sit beside local ones, and their tables filter, sort and export but stay read-only.

bands.title: Schema
text: Redshift has no indexes, enums, sequences or triggers to manage: DISTKEY and SORTKEY do an index’s work. From the sidebar, rename tables, databases and schemas, or create a schema with its owner.

bands.title: Monitor and back up
text: The Server Dashboard lists sessions and slow queries, cancels a query with pg_cancel_backend and ends a session with pg_terminate_backend, each after you confirm. Run VACUUM, ANALYZE and GRANT in the SQL editor.
<backup>Backup Dump and Restore Dump</backup> run {dumpTool} and pg_restore from your Mac, through the connection’s SSH tunnel when it has one. Install them first with Homebrew’s libpq.

moveData: <importData>Import</importData> loads {importFormats} files from your Mac into a Redshift table. Export writes tables, external ones included, or query results as {exportFormats}.
iphone: Bring the connection over with <icloudSync>iCloud Sync</icloudSync> ({icloudSyncTier} on the Mac) or an <share>exported connection file</share>. It runs on the PostgreSQL driver built into the app: browse tables as cards, filter and sort them, and run SQL in the Query tab.

faq.question: Does TablePro work with Redshift Serverless?
faq.answer: Yes. Put the workgroup endpoint in the host field and fill in the port, database and user as you would for a provisioned cluster.

faq.question: Does pg_dump support Redshift?
faq.answer: No pg_dump release claims to support the PostgreSQL version Redshift reports. TablePro runs the pg_dump you installed, so try a backup of a small schema before you rely on it.
